clue.text: Drone, brief solution for US?

definitions.note: a pronoun standing for people; the answer is the plural noun for them

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the word that follows loses its tail

blocks.note: a drone is a low continuous hum
a solution to a question is its answer

explanation.surface: Someone asks what an American would call a monotonous, short-winded fix.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drone' and 'US' look like a worker bee and America; the capitals hide the pronoun us, and ANSWER is clipped to ANS.
explanation.definitionFit: We, the speakers referred to as us, are people, members of the human species.

clue.text: Leader of unruly mob battered boss

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
something battered has been knocked out of shape, so the following word's letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the opening letter of unruly
taken as written before being rearranged

explanation.surface: A gang leader is beaten up by his own rowdy crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' suggests a gang chief, but here it is the raised centre of a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: An umbo is the round projecting knob at the centre of a shield, which is also called its boss.

clue.text: A new show holding a vote on old people

indicators.note: to hold something is to keep it inside, so the show wraps round what follows

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the standard abbreviation for new
a gloss is a superficial show or appearance
taken as written
a cross is marked on a ballot paper to vote
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fresh television programme is built around a ballot about the elderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old people' sounds like pensioners, but it means an ancient nation; a cross on a ballot paper is the conventional vote.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anglo-Saxons were the Germanic peoples who ruled England before the Norman Conquest of 1066.

clue.text: Engaged person OK to dance, embracing female

indicators.note: dancing moves things about, so the preceding letters are set in a new arrangement
to embrace is to wrap one's arms round, so the rearranged letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
F is the standard abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: An engaged person is allowed to dance while holding a woman close.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone already promised to a partner, or a thing already reserved, is said to be taken or claimed by another.

clue.text: Feeble way to refer to reversing

indicators.note: reversing means going backwards, so the word for refer to is read from right to left

blocks.note: a path is a way or track
to cite is to refer to or quote

explanation.surface: A weak manoeuvre in which a driver mentions backing up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something pitifully inadequate or weak is called pathetic in everyday speech.

clue.text: Usual meeting place not quite enough for social climber

indicators.note: falling a little short means the word stops before its final letter

blocks.note: par is the usual or normal standard
a venue is a place where people meet

explanation.surface: The regular haunt is too small for an ambitious newcomer to society.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is an upstart who has recently gained wealth or status but lacks the acceptance of those already there.

clue.text: Noise from guitar fret? Start to tune up

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept
in a down entry, going up means the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: the opening letter of tune
to fret something is to wear it away, as gnawing does

explanation.surface: A player wonders whether a buzzing guitar fret means it's time to tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fret' looks like the ridge on a guitar neck, but it is the verb meaning wear away; the question mark admits the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A twang is the sharp, ringing sound made by a plucked string, typical of a steel guitar.

clue.text: The purpose of open discussion

indicators.note: of here means made from, so the letters are taken from inside the next words

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Someone asks what an open debate is really for.
explanation.definitionFit: An end is an aim or goal, as in the phrase 'the end justifies the means'.

clue.text: Pub praises new product

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
an ovation is a show of praise

explanation.surface: A pub applauds the latest item on its menu.
explanation.definitionFit: An innovation is something newly introduced, such as a fresh invention or method.

clue.text: Please let me go or come again

blocks.note: first meaning: a polite request to be excused or allowed past
second meaning: a request to repeat what was said

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be released, or to have the words repeated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Come again' is informal for 'what did you say?', not an invitation to return.
explanation.definitionFit: This polite phrase serves both as an apology when brushing past someone and as a query when a remark was not heard.

clue.text: Famous runner carrying her stick

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so the runner wraps round the next word

blocks.note: Sebastian Coe, British Olympic middle-distance champion
taken as written

explanation.surface: A celebrated athlete holds a relay baton for a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Sebastian Coe won Olympic gold at 1500 metres in 1980 and 1984.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold together or adhere firmly, as particles do.

clue.text: Start broadcasting from, primarily, Golders Green

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: the opening letter of Golders
olive is a shade of green

explanation.surface: A radio station launches its programme from a North London suburb.
explanation.walkthrough: Golders Green is a district of north London; 'Green' is split off and read as a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: When a station or website goes live it begins transmitting or operating in real time.

clue.text: Spill jam, given flimsier sandwich

indicators.note: a sandwich has its filling between two slices, so the word for flimsier holds the jam

blocks.note: a flimsier excuse is a lamer one
a jam is a predicament or plight

explanation.surface: Someone spills jam on a sandwich that is thinner than it should be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spill' and 'jam' suggest an accident with preserves; a spill is a thin strip of wood or twisted paper used to light a lamp or pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamplighter is a taper or spill used to carry a flame to a lamp's wick.

clue.text: Do the first part of it?

definitions.text: Do the first part of it?

blocks.clueFragment: Do the first part of it?
blocks.note: surface reading: an instruction to carry out the opening stage of some task
setter's reading: do is a musical note, the first in the familiar singing scale

explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' reads as a verb, but it is the noun doh, the first syllable of the scale do-re-mi.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the system of teaching singing with syllables doh, ray, me, fah, soh, lah, te, beginning with doh.

clue.text: Hand over all evidence of monarch leaving throne?

blocks.note: first meaning: the poker hand that beats every other
second meaning, playful: the sound of a king pulling the chain after using the lavatory, jokingly called a throne

explanation.surface: A ruler abdicates and passes power over everything to a successor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand over' looks like a verb about surrendering power; it is a card hand that tops all others.
explanation.definitionFit: Ace, king, queen, jack and ten of one suit is the highest poker hand, unbeatable by any other.

clue.text: New horse boxes are affecting old landlord

indicators.note: something new is remade, so the following word's letters take a fresh order
to box something is to enclose it, so the rearranged letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written before being rearranged
things that tell have a marked effect, as in 'the strain began to tell'

explanation.surface: A fresh horse in its stable box is having an effect on a former publican.
explanation.definitionFit: In archaic use a hosteller was an innkeeper who lodged travellers, the keeper of a hostelry.

clue.text: Spymaster and worried colleague

blocks.note: M is James Bond's spymaster boss
something that worried you ate at you, as in 'what's eating him?'

explanation.surface: A spy chief and an anxious fellow agent.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate is a fellow worker or companion, as in a workmate or shipmate.

clue.text: Covering over swimming pool

blocks.note: a lid is a covering
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A cover is pulled over an outdoor pool.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool, especially in Britain.

clue.text: Fish and chopped nut on ice

indicators.note: chopped means cut short, so the word loses its final letter
on means placed after, so the shortened nut follows the ice

blocks.note: a drink on ice is served on the rocks
an almond is a nut

explanation.surface: A recipe lists fish together with chopped nuts served cold on ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fish and chopped nut' reads like a dish; 'and' just joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Rock salmon is a British fishmonger's name for dogfish and similar species sold for fish and chips.

clue.text: Old man cutting wire with skill

indicators.note: to cut into something is to go inside it, so the old man sits within the wire

blocks.note: a cable is a wire
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: An elderly man deftly snips through a wire.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone capable is competent and able, having the talent needed to do a job well.

clue.text: Gets through customs, then skyward

blocks.note: customs are usages or habits
skyward means upward

explanation.surface: A traveller clears passport control and then takes off in a plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gets through customs' suggests an airport; customs here means habits.
explanation.definitionFit: To get through supplies is to consume or exhaust them completely.

clue.text: Icy, or the opposite?

blocks.note: first meaning: freezing, like the regions round the poles
second meaning: diametrically contrary, as at opposite ends of the earth

explanation.walkthrough: 'Or the opposite?' seems to ask for a word meaning hot; instead the opposite is itself the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes both frozen arctic conditions and things that are complete contraries, as in 'polar opposites'.

clue.text: Word for one turning on soft, small light

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the abbreviation is read backwards
on means placed after, so the turned piece comes last

blocks.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
a light-emitting diode is a tiny electronic light
e.g. means for example, or for one

explanation.surface: Someone asks for the word for switching on a dim little lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving your word is making a promise, and a pledge is a solemn promise.

clue.text: Is able to house large family

indicators.note: to house something is to give it a home inside, so the first word surrounds the next

blocks.note: if someone can, they are able
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone has room to accommodate a big family.
explanation.definitionFit: A clan is an extended group of related households, especially in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: Taking a long time or a couple of minutes?

blocks.note: first meaning: gradually, in slow stages
second meaning, playful: minute read as tiny, two of them set side by side like a measurement

explanation.walkthrough: 'Minutes' looks like units of time but is the adjective meaning tiny, said twice, as in 'two by four'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means gradually or by degrees, and taken literally it is one small thing next to another small thing.

clue.text: When inverted, only water could be in it

indicators.note: turning upside down in a down entry means the word reads from bottom to top

blocks.note: but can mean only, as in 'she was but a child'

explanation.surface: An upturned container can hold nothing but water.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is a wide open container, such as a bathtub, which is filled with water.

clue.text: Crowd wave before English party

blocks.note: to jam is to crowd or cram together
a bore is a tidal wave surging up a river, like the Severn bore
E is the standard abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Fans do a Mexican wave before heading to an English celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamboree is a large lively gathering or celebration, such as a scouting rally.

clue.text: Eager artist’s group

blocks.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts
a ring is a group or gang, as in a spy ring

explanation.surface: A keen painter's circle of friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Raring, as in 'raring to go', describes someone very keen and impatient to start.
